questions.question: What is the full form of S3?

explanation.correct: S3 stands for Simple Storage Service — AWS's fully managed object storage.
explanation.why: A, C, and D are not AWS service names. S3 has stood for Simple Storage Service since its launch in 2006.

questions.question: What is the maximum object size you can store in S3?

explanation.correct: The maximum single object size in S3 is 5 TB (terabytes).
explanation.why: 5 GB is the maximum single PUT upload limit, not the max object size. S3 has a hard cap of 5 TB per object.

questions.question: What is the maximum file size you can upload in a single PUT operation to S3?

explanation.correct: The maximum single PUT upload limit is 5 GB. Files larger than 5 GB must use Multipart Upload.
explanation.why: 5 TB is the maximum object size, not the single PUT limit. 100 MB is AWS's recommendation to consider multipart, not the hard limit.

questions.question: Which S3 storage class is the default when you upload an object without specifying a class?

explanation.correct: S3 Standard is the default storage class — applied automatically if no class is specified.
explanation.why: Intelligent-Tiering and IA classes must be explicitly selected. Standard is chosen by default because it offers the best availability and performance.

questions.question: Which S3 storage class stores data in only ONE Availability Zone?

explanation.correct: S3 One Zone-IA is the only storage class that stores data in a single Availability Zone, making it cheaper but less resilient.
explanation.why: All other classes replicate data across a minimum of 3 AZs. One Zone-IA trades resilience for cost savings.

questions.question: What does S3 Versioning protect against?

options.text: Accidental deletion and overwriting of objects

explanation.correct: Versioning keeps multiple versions of the same object, allowing recovery from accidental deletions or overwrites.
explanation.why: Access control is handled by bucket policies and IAM. Replication is a separate feature. Versioning is specifically about data history and recovery.

questions.question: What is the durability level guaranteed by S3?

explanation.correct: S3 guarantees 11 nines of durability (99.999999999%), meaning data is almost impossible to lose even over centuries.
explanation.why: 11 nines is achieved by replicating data across multiple devices and facilities. This is one of the most commonly tested S3 facts.

questions.question: What is a 'bucket' in S3?

options.text: A virtual machine for running code
A top-level container for storing objects in a specific AWS region
A network interface for S3 access
A type of S3 storage class

explanation.correct: A bucket is the top-level container in S3. You create it in a specific region, and all objects inside live in that region.
explanation.why: EC2 runs code, not buckets. Storage classes categorize objects, not buckets. Network access is managed separately.

questions.question: What does Multipart Upload do in S3?

options.text: Uploads a file to multiple regions simultaneously
Splits a large file into chunks and uploads them in parallel for efficiency
Encrypts a file before uploading it
Compresses a file before storing it

explanation.correct: Multipart Upload splits a large file into smaller parts, uploads them in parallel, and S3 reassembles them as a single object.
explanation.why: Replication is a separate feature. Encryption is a separate S3 feature. Compression is not performed by S3 automatically.

questions.question: Which S3 storage class has NO retrieval fee?

explanation.correct: S3 Standard has no retrieval fee. S3 Intelligent-Tiering also has no retrieval fee. All IA and Glacier classes charge retrieval fees.
explanation.why: Standard-IA, One Zone-IA, and all Glacier classes charge a per-GB retrieval fee. S3 Standard is designed for frequent access so retrieval is free.

questions.question: What is a 'key' in the context of an S3 object?

options.text: An encryption key used to secure the object
The name (path) that uniquely identifies the object within a bucket
A permission token for accessing the object
The region code where the object is stored

explanation.correct: In S3, the 'key' is the name of the object, including any folder-like path structure. It uniquely identifies the object within a bucket.
explanation.why: Encryption uses separate KMS keys. Access uses IAM policies. The region is part of the bucket configuration, not the key.

questions.question: Where is an S3 bucket's data physically stored?

options.text: Globally distributed across all AWS regions
In the region you selected when creating the bucket
In the closest AWS region to your location
Automatically across all availability zones in all regions

explanation.correct: S3 data is stored in the specific region you choose when creating the bucket. It does not automatically replicate to other regions.
explanation.why: Cross-region replication is an opt-in feature. Data sovereignty and compliance often depend on this — data stays in your chosen region by default.

questions.question: What happens when you delete an object from an S3 bucket that has versioning ENABLED?

options.text: The object is permanently deleted immediately
The object is moved to the Recycle Bin for 30 days
A delete marker is placed on the object and it disappears from the main view
All versions of the object are deleted simultaneously

explanation.correct: With versioning enabled, deleting an object from the main view adds a delete marker — the object hides from view but all versions remain accessible in the versions tab.
explanation.why: Permanent deletion requires explicitly deleting individual versions. S3 does not have a Recycle Bin by default. Versioning protects each version independently.

questions.question: A company stores backup files that are accessed once every three months and need millisecond retrieval. Which storage class is MOST cost-effective?

explanation.correct: Glacier Instant Retrieval is designed for archive data accessed quarterly with millisecond retrieval — cheaper than Standard or Standard-IA for rarely accessed data.
explanation.why: S3 Standard is too expensive for quarterly access. Glacier Flexible takes minutes to hours to retrieve. Standard-IA is for monthly access, not quarterly.

questions.question: What is the minimum billable object size for S3 Standard-IA?

options.text: No minimum — billed for actual size

explanation.correct: S3 Standard-IA has a minimum billable object size of 128 KB. Even a 1 KB file stored in Standard-IA is billed as 128 KB.
explanation.why: S3 Standard has no minimum. 128 KB applies to Standard-IA and One Zone-IA. This is a common exam trick on cost optimization questions.

questions.question: You upload a 10 GB file to S3 using the console. What happens automatically?

options.text: The upload fails because 10 GB exceeds the maximum object size
S3 automatically uses Multipart Upload to split and upload the file in chunks
S3 compresses the file to under 5 GB before uploading
The file is uploaded in Standard storage class only

explanation.correct: Files larger than 5 GB automatically trigger Multipart Upload. S3 splits the file into parts, uploads them in parallel, and reassembles them.
explanation.why: 10 GB is well within the 5 TB object size limit. S3 does not compress files. Storage class can still be chosen for large files.

questions.question: Which S3 storage class automatically monitors access patterns and moves objects to cost-optimized tiers?

explanation.correct: S3 Intelligent-Tiering monitors each object's access patterns and automatically moves it between Frequent Access, Infrequent Access, and Archive tiers.
explanation.why: Standard and Standard-IA are fixed-tier storage classes. Glacier Flexible does not monitor access — it is a static archive class.

questions.question: What is the minimum storage duration for S3 Standard-IA?

explanation.correct: S3 Standard-IA has a 30-day minimum storage duration. If you delete an object before 30 days, you are still charged for the full 30 days.
explanation.why: 30 days applies to Standard-IA and One Zone-IA. 90 days applies to Glacier Instant and Glacier Flexible. 180 days applies to Deep Archive.

questions.question: How do you RESTORE an accidentally deleted object in a versioning-enabled S3 bucket?

options.text: Contact AWS Support to restore the object
Click the 'Undo Delete' button in the S3 console
Select and delete the delete marker in the versions view
Enable MFA Delete and attempt recovery

explanation.correct: To restore a deleted object in a versioning-enabled bucket, go to the versions view, select the delete marker, and delete it. The object automatically reappears in the main view.
explanation.why: AWS Support cannot recover objects for you. There is no 'Undo Delete' button in S3. MFA Delete adds protection but is not a recovery mechanism.

questions.question: What is the key difference between S3 Standard-IA and S3 One Zone-IA?

options.text: Standard-IA supports versioning, One Zone-IA does not
Standard-IA stores data across multiple AZs, One Zone-IA stores in a single AZ
Standard-IA has no retrieval fee, One Zone-IA charges for retrieval
One Zone-IA has a higher durability than Standard-IA

explanation.correct: Standard-IA replicates data across 3+ AZs for resilience. One Zone-IA uses only 1 AZ, making it cheaper but at higher risk if that AZ fails.
explanation.why: Both classes support versioning and both charge retrieval fees. Standard-IA has higher availability due to multi-AZ replication.

questions.question: What is the minimum storage duration for S3 Glacier Deep Archive?

explanation.correct: Glacier Deep Archive has a 180-day minimum storage duration — the longest of all S3 storage classes.
explanation.why: 30 days is Standard-IA. 90 days is Glacier Instant and Glacier Flexible. Deep Archive at 180 days reflects its use for multi-year retention workloads.

questions.question: A company needs to store financial records for 10 years and ensure NOBODY — not even the root account — can delete or modify them. Which S3 feature and mode should they use?

options.text: S3 Object Lock in Governance mode
S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode
S3 Bucket Policy with Deny Delete

explanation.correct: S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode prevents ANY user — including the AWS root account — from deleting or modifying the object until the retention period expires.
explanation.why: Governance mode allows bypass by privileged users. MFA Delete protects versioned objects but does not prevent root account actions. Bucket policies can be modified by admins.

questions.question: Which statement about S3 Intelligent-Tiering is TRUE?

options.text: It charges a retrieval fee when you access data from the archive tiers
It charges a per-object monitoring and automation fee
Objects never move to archive tiers automatically
It requires manual configuration to move objects between tiers

explanation.correct: S3 Intelligent-Tiering charges a small per-object monitoring and automation fee each month, which is how it pays for the intelligence to track and move objects.
explanation.why: Intelligent-Tiering has NO retrieval fee. Objects do move to archive tiers automatically after 90+ days of no access. Everything is automatic — no manual configuration.

questions.question: An object is uploaded to an S3 bucket with versioning enabled. Later, versioning is SUSPENDED. What happens to existing versions?

options.text: All existing versions are deleted immediately
Existing versions are preserved; new uploads overwrite without creating new versions
The bucket is locked and no new uploads are allowed
Versioning cannot be suspended once enabled

explanation.correct: Suspending versioning preserves all existing versions but stops creating new version IDs for future uploads. New uploads overwrite the current version.
explanation.why: Versions are never automatically deleted by suspending. Versioning can be suspended (though not fully disabled). The bucket remains writable after suspension.

questions.question: What is the difference between a delete marker and permanently deleting a version in S3?

options.text: There is no difference — both remove the object permanently
A delete marker hides the object from the main view; permanently deleting a specific version removes it forever
A delete marker permanently removes the object; version deletion only hides it
Delete markers only apply to Glacier storage classes

explanation.correct: A delete marker is a soft delete — the object hides from the main view but all versions remain. Deleting a specific version from the versions view is irreversible.
explanation.why: This is a critical distinction for accidental deletion recovery. Delete markers can be removed to restore objects. Permanently deleted versions cannot be recovered.

questions.question: A startup stores user profile pictures. Images from the last 30 days are accessed daily. Images from 31–365 days are rarely accessed. Images over 1 year are never accessed. Which combination of storage classes optimizes cost?

options.text: S3 Standard → S3 Standard-IA → S3 Glacier Deep Archive with lifecycle policies
S3 One Zone-IA for all images to minimize cost

explanation.correct: Lifecycle policies can automatically transition images: Standard for recent (daily access), Standard-IA for 31–365 days (infrequent), and Deep Archive for 1+ years (never accessed, cheapest).
explanation.why: All-Standard wastes money. All-Intelligent-Tiering adds monitoring fees. One Zone-IA for all images risks data loss since profile pictures are irreplaceable. The lifecycle policy approach is the AWS Well-Architected recommendation.

questions.question: What is an S3 Legal Hold?

options.text: A government regulation requiring S3 data to be stored locally
An Object Lock setting that prevents deletion without a fixed retention period, active until explicitly removed
A billing hold placed on an account when S3 costs exceed a threshold
A way to lock a bucket so no new objects can be uploaded

explanation.correct: A Legal Hold prevents an object from being deleted or modified without a retention period — it stays active until explicitly removed by a user with s3:PutObjectLegalHold permission.
explanation.why: Legal Hold is commonly used in litigation scenarios where data must be preserved regardless of any pre-configured retention period.

questions.question: You must use Multipart Upload for objects larger than which size?

explanation.correct: Multipart Upload is REQUIRED for objects larger than 5 GB. It is recommended (but not required) for objects larger than 100 MB for better performance.
explanation.why: 100 MB is a recommendation, not a requirement. 5 TB is the max object size. The hard requirement kicks in at 5 GB for a single PUT upload.

questions.question: Which S3 storage class is MOST appropriate for data that is accessed once a year for audit purposes?

explanation.correct: Glacier Flexible Retrieval is ideal for archive data accessed once a year where retrieval can take minutes to hours. It costs far less than Standard or Standard-IA for such infrequent access.
explanation.why: Standard is overkill for annual access. Standard-IA is for monthly access. Glacier Instant is for quarterly access. Glacier Flexible matches annual/less-frequent access patterns.

questions.question: A bucket name must be globally unique across all AWS. Why?

options.text: AWS billing requires unique identifiers per customer
The bucket name is part of every object's URL, which must be globally resolvable
Unique names prevent IAM policy conflicts across accounts
S3 replication requires unique bucket names to avoid circular replication

explanation.correct: Because the bucket name appears in every object's public URL (e.g., bucket-name.s3.region.amazonaws.com/key), it must be globally unique so URLs can be resolved correctly anywhere on the internet.
explanation.why: IAM policies use ARNs, not names. Replication uses separate configuration. The URL resolution requirement is the fundamental reason for global uniqueness.
